final_candidates.decision_summary: Asp187 sits at the stalk-head junction (185-187 helix) implicated in G-F fusion triggering; removing the negative charge may enhance F activation. Strongest all-around evidence: neutral ESM-1v (1.0), favorable ProteinMPNN delta (+3.29), and nonzero mutant frequency in homologs.

Asp485 is in the C-terminal lobe near the ephrin-contacting region, so charge removal could tune receptor-mediated triggering with modest affinity-loss risk. Near-neutral ESM (0.999) and acceptable MPNN (0.70); discounted for weak MSA coverage (app 0.33).

Lys176 lies at the base of the globular head where conformational signals propagate to F; conservative Lys->Gln neutralizes charge without drastic size change. Neutral ESM and acceptable structure compatibility (0.80), lowered slightly by zero homolog frequency.

stop_reason.detail: Evidence across all available informative dimensions already discriminates the pool and additional calls are unlikely to alter the Top-3 ranking.

history.rationale: Terminal residue substitution near the receptor-binding rim that could modestly alter receptor affinity.

C-terminal residue is solvent-exposed and far from the ephrin-binding pocket/F-triggering stalk, so it is unlikely to strongly change entry; keep only as a low-priority control-like candidate pending evidence.

Extreme C-terminal residue with only 2/21 homolog coverage (app 0.095) and no plausible mechanistic link to receptor engagement or F-triggering; T->S is essentially neutral and unlikely to improve entry.

rejection.reason: Extreme C-terminal residue with only 2/21 homolog coverage (app 0.095) and no plausible mechanistic link to receptor engagement or F-triggering; T->S is essentially neutral and unlikely to improve entry.

history.rationale: Asp187 (L186-D187-R188 verified) sits at the stalk/head junction implicated in paramyxovirus G-F fusion triggering; removing a negative charge may alter stalk-head coupling that controls F activation.

Best all-around profile: ESM-1v neutral (1.0), strongly favorable ProteinMPNN delta (+3.29) at the stalk-head junction helix (185-187), and nonzero mutant frequency in homologs. Junction location is directly implicated in F-triggering, fitting the entry-efficiency objective.

Lys176 (S175-K176-Q177 verified) lies at the base of the globular head where conformational signals propagate to F; charge-neutralizing Lys->Gln can modulate head-stalk interface without drastic size change.
ESM-1v neutral and acceptable structure compatibility (0.80); zero MSA frequency slightly lowers support but K->Q is chemically conservative at the head base where trigger signals propagate.
Arg302 (V301-R302-T303 verified) is on the beta-propeller surface near the receptor-binding face; tuning surface charge there can change ephrin-B2/B3 engagement kinetics and downstream entry.
Structure compatibility is clearly poor (ΔlogP=-4.89) and Leu never appears in homologs, so despite a neutral ESM score the viability risk on the receptor-binding face is too high for top ranking.

Asp309 (N308-D309-S310 verified) is in the 306-311 loop contributing to the receptor-binding ridge in related henipavirus G structures; Ala is a minimally disruptive perturbation to test affinity/trigger balance.
Moderate structure compatibility (0.73) but notably reduced ESM plausibility (0.598) and no homolog support in a flexible, high-B-factor turn; retained as mid-tier backup only.

Asp485 (E484-D485-T486 verified) is in the C-terminal lobe of the head close to the ephrin-contacting region; charge removal could enhance receptor-mediated triggering, though risk of affinity loss exists.
Near-neutral ESM (0.999) and acceptable MPNN (0.70) in the receptor-proximal C-terminal lobe; MSA support is weak due to low coverage (app 0.33) so it is discounted rather than rejected.
